profile.summary: RFD4-Proteina designs proteins and biomolecular complexes, generating sequence and all-atom structure together rather than a backbone to be sequenced later. The design is specified either as an annotated CIF structure or as a short YAML condition spec, which can fix a motif, name hotspots, hold a binding target or a ligand, or constrain features such as burial and hydrogen bonds. One model covers monomers, protein and DNA binders, antibodies and nanobodies, enzyme motif scaffolding and small molecule pockets, and it can also refine an existing design by partial diffusion or search over generation paths scored by structure prediction oracles. It is a flow matching model in the latent space of a frozen autoencoder, so generation always loads two matched checkpoints. Code and weights are BSD 3-Clause, from the Baker Lab and NVIDIA GenAIR.

summary_quotes.text:
RFD4-Proteina designs proteins and biomolecular complexes with sequence–structure co-design,
motif and binding-site conditioning, partial diffusion, and reward-guided search.
**Many design tasks from one model:** monomers, protein and DNA binders, antibodies and nanobodies, enzymes and motif scaffolding, small-molecule pockets.

It generates protein sequences and all-atom structures together, conditioned on the molecular context you want to preserve: a binding target, an enzyme motif, a ligand, or selected structural features.

RFD4-Proteina always loads **two** checkpoints together to generate: a denoiser and the
autoencoder it was trained against.
A flow-matching foundation model for biomolecular design — Baker Lab × NVIDIA GenAIR

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Two components are always loaded together. The autoencoder is frozen and unified: one encoder and decoder covering proteins, nucleic acids, DNA and modified residues, with 32 latent channels per residue and a residue vocabulary of 147 classes, trained to 400,000 steps. The denoiser is a flow matching latent model that generates in exactly that latent space, which is why the pair cannot be mixed across releases: the developers say mixing a flow model with a different autoencoder produces nonsense rather than an error. The released denoiser is a pretrained base at step 320,000 with a rank-32 LoRA fine-tune merged in, and by default it conditions the decoder on its own sequence readout during inference. Sampling runs 60 steps, with the trunk recycled a varying number of times per step: the three released presets, low, medium and high, come to 120, 180 and 300 trunk passes, medium being the default. Reward-guided search branches and prunes candidates at points in that schedule, scored by a refolding oracle such as OpenFold3.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The current release is the 2026-10-19 pair: rfd4-proteina-flow-release-2026-10-19 as the denoiser and rfd4-proteina-ae-release-2026-10-19 as the autoencoder, published under the stable names flow_checkpoints/rfd4_proteina_flow-ema.ckpt and ae_checkpoints/rfd4_proteina_ae-ema.ckpt, with SHA-256 sidecars and a release manifest. It supersedes the 2026-10-15 pair, which shared the architecture, and an earlier pair with a 16-dimensional latent and a 33-class vocabulary which is incompatible. The pretrained base and the LoRA adapter are published separately under base/ and adapter/, and the root bundle is exactly the two merged. The published checkpoints carry EMA weights and hyperparameters only, which is enough for inference or fine-tuning but not to resume a training run. Per release-checkpoints.json the released flow checkpoint is 1,751,488,703 bytes against 3,511,389,403 for its full training checkpoint, and the autoencoder 1,029,340,246 against 3,095,456,721. The model card states 1.74 GB and 4.21 GB for the flow pair, which does not match its own manifest: 4,211,265,195 bytes is the full size of a different file, flow_checkpoints/rfd4_proteina_flow_pretrain-ema.ckpt, and 1,742,660,596 is the size of model.safetensors. Reproducibility comes from pinning: configs/inference.yaml names the Hub repository and the revision, from_pretrained takes a revision argument, and the documentation tells users not to hard-code filenames anywhere else.

sections.title: What the developers claim, and how they qualify it
sections.body: The model card reports design efficiency as structurally distinct computational passers per GPU-hour, including generation and evaluation, on four internal benchmarks: 71.60 on 24 protein binder targets against 13.24 for the best comparator, 112.25 on 77 small-molecule binder targets against 15.48, 91.18 on 37 atomic motif enzyme targets against 26.02, and 41.97 on three DNA binder targets against 9.46. The developers attach three qualifications themselves. The numbers were measured on the previous release pair in a frozen benchmark of 9 October 2026 and have not been re-measured on the current checkpoints. The conditioning differs between methods in some comparisons, and only three DNA targets are included. And computational passers do not establish experimental activity.

quotes.text: **Metric:** mean per-target structurally distinct computational passers per GPU-hour, including generation and common AF3 evaluation.

run_guide.summary: Install from PyPI with uv, describe a PD-L1 binder in a short YAML spec, and generate with the released weights from the Hugging Face Hub.
prerequisites: Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, an NVIDIA GPU from the tested list and a CUDA 13-compatible driver. macOS and Windows are not supported.
About 7 GB for the environment and about 1.7 GB for the weights bundle, cached under HF_HOME.
Network access to the Hugging Face Hub. The repositories are public, so no token is needed; a restricted repository needs HF_TOKEN or hf auth login.
Nothing extra for generation. Refolding metrics and reward-guided search need an AlphaFold 2 or OpenFold3 environment, installed separately.
BSD 3-Clause terms for the model, the weights and the code; the optional refolding images have their own terms.
